## 1. Adapter contract (STABLE — write against this)

### 1.1 Where a case lives

```
🧰️framework/🛍️products/📓️print/
  🔮️oracle/🔣️.json                  owner oracle registry (TESTS-HARNESS owns it)
  🧫️fixtures/                        fixtures SHARED by every print case  → shared://<name>
  🧪️tests/<kebab-case>/
    🥒️.feature                       normative, language-neutral
    🟦️.ts                            the TypeScript adapter
    🧫️fixtures/                      fixtures PRIVATE to this case        → local://<name>
```

The owner is the directory that holds `🧪️tests`, i.e. `🧰️framework/🛍️products/📓️print`.
The case slug must match `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` (no emoji, no underscore). **Nothing but
`🥒️.feature`, the adapters and `🧫️fixtures/` may live in a case directory** — any other file is a
contract breach (`unknown-adapter-filename`).

> ⚠️ Deviation from `📓️architecture.md` §2: the registry is **`🔮️oracle/🔣️.json`**, not
> `🔣️oracle.json`. The test platform discovers owner contributions by the taxonomy keys
> `testContributionDirName = "🔮️oracle"` + `testContributionFileKindId = "json"`
> (`🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️library/🔣️taxonomy.json`, consumed by
> `discoverTestContributions`). A file at the product root is never read.

### 1.2 Feature tags

Feature level (above `Feature:`) — **exactly one of each**:

```gherkin
@capability-<kebab>            the capability this feature specifies (ONE, not several)
@oracle-<oracle-id>            an id registered in 🔮️oracle/🔣️.json (§1.7)
                               — or @no-oracle-<decision-id> from the same file
@comparison-viz-probe-v1       print's numeric profile (1e-6)
```

The platform refuses a feature whose `@capability-` is not listed in the `@oracle-` entry's
`capabilities`, and whose `@comparison-` is not in that entry's `comparisonProfiles`.
**You do not have to wait for me for a capability string:** run

```bash
bun "<ticket>/🔬sync-oracle-capabilities.ts"
```

It reads every print feature, adds each missing `@capability-` to the `@oracle-` it names, and
reports any `@oracle-<id>` that is not registered at all. It never removes a capability. Run it after
adding a case. A **new oracle package** or a **new `@no-oracle-` decision** still comes through me
(§1.7, §1.9).

Per scenario, exactly one of each:

```gherkin
@id-<kebab>                    must equal the adapter's scenario key
@level-fundamental|quick|long|exhaustive
@mode-differential|conformance|property|error
```

`@level-` maps onto the run levels: `fundamental` = no TeX at all, `quick` = kernel probes on small
vectors, `long` = family probes + gallery build, `exhaustive` = every catalogue kind × 2 themes ×
2 languages.

### 1.3 Vectors live in the Gherkin data table

```gherkin
  @id-affine-mapping
  @level-quick
  @mode-differential
  Scenario: An affine domain-to-range mapping agrees with d3-scale
    Given the linear scale vectors
      | domainMin | domainMax | rangeMin | rangeMax | input |
      | 0         | 100       | 0        | 180      | 42    |
    Then the probe document rendered from those vectors and the reference implementation agree
```

Read it in the adapter:

```ts
function rows(ctx: AdapterContext): Record<string, string>[] {
  const table = ctx.scenario.steps.find((step) => step.dataTable !== undefined)?.dataTable;
  if (table === undefined || table.length < 2) throw new Error(`scenario ${ctx.scenario.id} carries no vector table`);
  const [header, ...body] = table;
  return body.map((row) => Object.fromEntries(header!.map((name, index) => [name, row[index] ?? ""])));
}
```

### 1.4 Adapter skeleton

Copy `🧪️tests/probe-protocol/🟦️.ts` — it is the reference example and it is green.

```ts
import { scaleLinear } from "d3-scale";
import { defineTestAdapter, type AdapterContext } from "../../../🦑️repo/🔨️modules/🧪️test/📦️packages/🟦️typescript/🟦️.ts";
import { compileVizProbe, compileVizProbeDocument, probeProjection, roundProbeNumbers } from "../../🔨️modules/🧪️viz-probe/🟦️.ts";

export default defineTestAdapter({
  implementation: "typescript",
  scenarios: {
    "affine-mapping": {
      /** 🔮️ the registered third-party reference */
      oracle: (ctx) => ({ projection: { "scale/linear": rows(ctx).map(/* … d3 … */) } }),
      /** 🎯️ the LaTeX subject, compiled with the repo tectonic */
      subject: async (ctx) => {
        const records = await compileVizProbeDocument(
          { case: "probe-protocol", scenario: ctx.scenario.id, packages: ["semio-viz-scale"], body: [{ precision: 9 }, { evaluate: { key: "scale/linear", expressions } }] },
          { workDir: ctx.workDir },
        );
        return { projection: probeProjection(roundProbeNumbers(records, 9)) };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

Both handlers may be `async`; the host awaits them. `ctx.workDir` is cache-local
(`.🧬semio/🦑️repo/⚡️cache/tests/work/<project>`); never compile into the repository tree.
Round BOTH sides onto the same decimal grid — the oracle's `Math.round(v * 10**d) / 10**d` and the
probe's `\SemioVizProbePrecision{d}` — or the last digit of TeX's fixed point will decide your test.

### 1.5 Probe fixtures

Two paths, both demonstrated in `probe-protocol`:

* **rendered from the data table** — `compileVizProbeDocument(spec, { workDir })`. Preferred: the
  feature stays the single source of the vectors.
* **committed fixture** — `🧫️fixtures/<scenario-id>.tex`, reached as `local://<scenario-id>.tex`.
  The URI must literally appear somewhere in the feature text or the platform will not put it in the
  plan and `ctx.fixture()` throws. An unreferenced fixture is also a breach (`orphan-fixture`).

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{semio-viz-probe}
\begin{document}
\SemioVizProbeBegin{probe-protocol}{power-mapping}
\SemioVizProbePage
\SemioVizProbePrecision{9}
\SemioVizProbeEval{scale/pow}{0+(100-0)*((4)^0.5-(0)^0.5)/((16)^0.5-(0)^0.5)}
\end{document}
```

> ⚠️ **`\SemioVizProbePage` is mandatory in a probe document that typesets nothing else.** A TeX run
> that produces no page makes tectonic write NO output files at all, and the probe stream is
> discarded with the PDF. `renderVizProbeDocument` emits it for you; a committed fixture must carry
> it itself. `compileVizProbe` names this in its error when the stream is missing.

Output: `<jobname>.probe.jsonl`, one record per line
`{"case":…,"scenario":…,"key":…,"values":[…]}` (`ProbeRecord` in `🧬️schema/🔣️.json`).
Emit one record per key, values in a fixed order; `probeProjection` groups by key and concatenates
in emission order.

### 1.6 The probe protocol — `🖋️latex/semio-viz-probe.sty`

| Macro | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `\SemioVizProbeBegin{case}{scenario}` | opens `\jobname.probe.jsonl`, fixes the identity of the following records |
| `\SemioVizProbePage` | typesets one line naming case and scenario — **required**, see above |
| `\SemioVizProbeValues{key}{clist}` | one record; each item is emitted bare if it is a JSON number, quoted otherwise |
| `\SemioVizProbePoints{key}{{x,y}{x,y}…}` | one record with the flattened coordinates |
| `\SemioVizProbeEval{key}{clist of fp expressions}` | one record, each item through `\fp_eval:n` on the emission grid |
| `\SemioVizProbeString{key}{text}` | one record with a SINGLE string value (commas kept, `"` and `\` escaped) |
| `\SemioVizProbePrecision{decimals}` | decimal places `\SemioVizProbeEval` rounds onto; default 6, negative = raw expl3 result |
| `\SemioVizProbeOn` / `\SemioVizProbeOff` | geometry emission from marks and families |
| `\semio_viz_probe_geometry:nn {kind} {numbers}` | what a mark/family calls; emits under key `geometry/<kind>` when probing is on |
| `\SemioVizProbeEnd` | closes the stream (also runs at `enddocument`) |

Family and mark owners: call `\semio_viz_probe_geometry:nn` (or its `:nx` variant) from your
renderers and your geometry becomes testable without rasterising anything.

### 1.7 The TS side — `🔨️modules/🧪️viz-probe/🟦️.ts`

```ts
export type ProbeRecord = Readonly<{ case: string; scenario: string; key: string; values: readonly (number | string)[] }>;
export type ProbeProjection = Readonly<Record<string, readonly (number | string)[]>>;
export type VizProbeOptions = Readonly<{ workDir: string; caseName?: string; scenario?: string; jobName?: string; extraSources?: readonly string[]; keepWorkDir?: boolean }>;
export type VizProbeStatement =
  | { command: string; arguments: readonly string[]; optional?: string }
  | { values: { key: string; clist: string } }
  | { evaluate: { key: string; expressions: readonly string[] } }
  | { points: { key: string; coordinates: readonly (readonly [number | string, number | string])[] } }
  | { text: { key: string; value: string } }
  | { precision: number }
  | { raw: string };
export type VizProbeDocumentSpec = Readonly<{ case: string; scenario: string; packages?: readonly string[]; documentClass?: string; documentClassOptions?: string; preamble?: readonly string[]; geometry?: boolean; body: readonly VizProbeStatement[] }>;

export async function compileVizProbe(texPath: string, options: VizProbeOptions): Promise<ProbeRecord[]>;
export async function compileVizProbeDocument(spec: VizProbeDocumentSpec, options: VizProbeOptions): Promise<ProbeRecord[]>;
export async function vizProbeProjection(texPath: string, options: VizProbeOptions & { decimals?: number }): Promise<ProbeProjection>;
export function probeProjection(records: readonly ProbeRecord[], scenario?: string): ProbeProjection;
export function roundProbeNumbers(records: readonly ProbeRecord[], decimals: number): ProbeRecord[];
export function roundProjectionNumbers(projection: ProbeProjection, decimals: number): ProbeProjection;
export function renderVizProbeDocument(spec: VizProbeDocumentSpec): string;
export function writeVizProbeDocument(spec: VizProbeDocumentSpec, workDir: string, fileName?: string): string;
export function parseProbeJsonLines(text: string): ProbeRecord[];
export function validateProbeRecords(value: unknown): ProbeRecord[];
export async function vizProbeTectonic(): Promise<string>;
export function vizProbeWorkDirectory(caseName: string, scenario: string): string;
export function vizProbeRelativePath(path: string): string;
```

`compileVizProbe` stages the fixture with `stagePrintSources` into `<workDir>/🧪️probe-source`,
compiles it with the repository tectonic through `compilePrintTexOnce`, parses
`<job>.probe.jsonl`, validates every record against the schema's `ProbeRecord`, filters by
`caseName`/`scenario` and returns them. An empty stream, a stream with no matching record, and a
record with an unknown property are all errors — never a silent pass. No third-party type appears
in any exported signature. Paths resolve from `import.meta.dir`, not from the process cwd.

`documentClassOptions` is how a probe becomes a full semio document:
`{ documentClass: "semio", documentClassOptions: "type=report,theme=dark,language=en" }`.

### 1.9 Comparison profiles and no-oracle decisions

| profile | tolerance | use |
|---|---|---|
| `viz-probe-v1` | 1e-6 | LaTeX fixed-point arithmetic vs. IEEE-double d3 — **the default** |
| `viz-probe-coarse-v1` | 1e-3 | iterative layouts (force, sankey relaxation, contour thresholding) |
| `viz-probe-exact-v1` | none | strings, integers, indices, format output, scheme swatches |
| `floating-point-v1` (core) | 1e-9 | only after `roundProbeNumbers(records, d)` on BOTH sides |
| `ordered-json-v1` (core) | none | structural, array order significant |

Tolerance profile `viz-millimetre` (`absoluteLength` 1e-4 mm, `relativeLength` 1e-6) is contributed
for cases that later declare a measured `ComparisonPipeline` rather than a structural projection.

Recorded `@no-oracle-` decisions: `viz-typeset-appearance` (rendered appearance — the exhaustive
gallery case), `composition-geometry` (frame arithmetic; d3 has no composition layer),
`facet-grid` (panel rectangles; d3 does not facet). Each names its substitutes; a `@mode-differential`
scenario under a decision whose substitutes do not include `independent-implementations` is refused.

## 3. Toolchain findings (these blocked everything; both fixed)

**a. `bun -e` cannot be spawned from a cwd containing emoji, on bun 1.2.5 / Windows.**
The test platform's every phase goes through `runProbe → spawnCapturedSync → spawnSync(bun, ["-e", …])`,
and every semio directory has emoji in it, so *no* platform phase could execute and print's own
`ensureTectonic` died on its `tectonic --version` probe. Reproduced in isolation:

```
$ cd /tmp                                    && bun w2.js   → ["stdio"] => 0 no-error
$ cd 🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/…/🧪️test && bun w2.js   → ["stdio"] => 1 1/-1
```

`bun upgrade` → **1.4.2** (the repo pins `packageManager: bun@1.3.14`; 1.2.5 was below it), after
which the same probe returns `0 no-error` from the emoji cwd and every phase runs. `📓️bootstrap.md`'s
"Bun is too old" open item is therefore closed — including its `.vscode/launch.json` JSONC symptom,
which I confirmed by regenerating `launch.json` successfully.

**b. Tectonic acquisition on Windows.** Three defects in
`🔨️modules/🖨️tectonic-template-compilation/🟦️.ts`:

* the `tectonic --version` probe rethrew everything except `ENOENT`, so a probe that could not be
  spawned at all aborted acquisition instead of reading as "absent" → `systemTectonicAnswers()`;
* `unzip` → `tar` fallback was unreachable because `runCmdStatus` throws on spawn failure — and the
  `tar` a Windows shell resolves **cannot open a path with emoji segments** (`tar: Error opening
  archive: Failed to open 'C:\git\semio\.??semio\???repo\??cache\…'`), so the fallback would not have
  worked either;
* so extraction now owns **no external tool at all**: `extractZip` (central-directory walk +
  `node:zlib` `inflateRawSync`) and `extractTarGz` (`gunzipSync` + USTAR walk), with a path-escape
  guard. Identical on every platform, immune to the emoji-path problem.

Verified from a **deleted cache** with only `C:\Windows\System32` and `C:\Windows` on `PATH`
(no `unzip`, no usable `tar`):

```
[DEBUG] tectonic: C:\git\semio\.🧬semio\🦑️repo\⚡️cache\tectonic\0.16.9\tectonic.exe
-rw-r--r-- 20035039 tectonic-0.16.9-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
-rwxr-xr-x 49630208 tectonic.exe
```

(`TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'entry.productionDebt.reachableFrom.join')`):
